$comment: The recovery conformance registry. Each entry is destroyed with a real SIGKILL against a real child process, not a simulated one: scripts/recovery.ts spawns the API, kills it at a chosen instant, starts a different process against the same database, and asserts what survived. Adding a scenario here without implementing it fails the run. The adversarial suite's A9 and A10 assert the same invariants against rewound state, which is faster and proves the recovery logic given a state; these prove a real crash produces that state.

scenarios.title: SIGKILL after the claim, before the payment
scenarios.threat: A crash between committing the execution claim and the money moving leaves authority spendable again.
scenarios.precondition: A single-use grant, an ALLOW, and a provider that records its arrival to its own committed ledger and then blocks forever.
scenarios.attack: Wait until the provider's ledger shows the request arrived, SIGKILL the whole process group, start a different process against the same database, and retry.
scenarios.expected_invariant: 409 EXECUTION_UNRESOLVED. The provider is not contacted again, its ledger is unchanged, the grant is still consumed, the original idempotency key is preserved, and the claim is listed for reconciliation.
cases: claim committed and externally visible before the provider was reached
grant consumed in the same transaction as the claim
provider not contacted a second time

scenarios.title: SIGKILL after the payment, before settlement
scenarios.threat: The money moved and the record of it did not. A retry pays twice.
scenarios.precondition: The same, with a provider that records the payment to its own committed ledger before blocking.
scenarios.attack: Wait until the ledger shows EXECUTED, SIGKILL the process group, restart, and retry.
scenarios.expected_invariant: 409 EXECUTION_UNRESOLVED -- never REPLAY_DETECTED, which would tell the caller the work is finished, and never a fresh execution. Scrutexity cannot distinguish this from R1 from its own records, and must not try: both answers are the same because the correct action is the same.
cases: money confirmed moved in the provider's own ledger
provider not contacted a second time
external state unchanged by the refused retry
idempotency key preserved so reconciliation asks about the same payment

scenarios.title: Control: no kill, the same path settles
scenarios.threat: The harness proves nothing if the path it kills never worked in the first place.
scenarios.precondition: The same setup with the provider configured not to block.
scenarios.attack: Execute normally, then retry against the settled claim.
scenarios.expected_invariant: 201 EXECUTED, then 200 with replayed: true. The provider is contacted exactly once. A settled claim replays its outcome, so the 409s in R1 and R2 are the crash state speaking rather than a blanket refusal to retry.
